summary: Tested user management (admin CRUD, roles, active toggle, set password, delete, self/last-admin protections), RBAC (403 on /api/users* and PUT /api/settings, nav hidden, /utenti redirect, Settings read-only), forgot-password (generic message, hashed token, real Resend send 202, rate limit 3/h) and reset-password (validation, valid single-use, invalid/expired tokens) via 23 pytest tests + 4 Playwright flows. All passed. Light regression OK: login/logout, dashboard, attive/passive/anagrafiche pages load.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout key uses request.client.host, which is the ingress/pod IP (seen 10.201.1.194 and 10.201.4.160 for the same client). Failed-attempt counters are split across ingress IPs, so an attacker gets about 5 x N attempts and lockout is inconsistent (7 bad attempts gave 7x 401 and no 429). Use the first X-Forwarded-For IP, or key on email alone.

If send_email fails (502/503/500), the error is returned only for registered emails, which reveals which emails exist. The token is also already inserted and counts toward the 3/h limit. Catch the error, log it, still return the generic message, and/or insert the token only after a successful send.

Existing sessions stay valid after a password reset or after an admin sets a password (stateless JWT, refresh token valid 7 days). login_attempts lockout is not cleared on reset. Consider a token_version/password_changed_at check.
The deleted user's password_reset_tokens are not removed (orphans remain until TTL).
Only resets the password. It does not force role=admin/active=true on an existing admin doc.

issues: Sonner toast (top-right) covers the 'Nuovo utente' button for a few seconds after every action

action_items: Use the real client IP (X-Forwarded-For) or an email-only key for login lockout
Make forgot-password always return the generic message even if the email send fails
Optional: invalidate sessions after a password reset/change; delete reset tokens when a user is deleted
critical_code_review_comments: pytest.ini enables xdist (-n --dist loadscope). Stateful test classes need -n 0 or the same scope. Run test_users_auth.py with -n 0.
Users page has no loading/error state on the initial GET /users (load() has no catch).

success_rate.backend: 100% (22 passed, 1 skipped because the 3/h rate limit was reached after the first run, which itself sent successfully)
